5. The mobile relocation office will be utilized in the project area if the need arises, particularly if it is found that people desire additional contact with relocation personnel.
6. Assistance will be offered to complete claims for moving and supplemental payments for which each displace may be eligible.
The Wisconsin Division of Highways recognizes that the proposed project will require the displacement of people and buildings. Every effort will be made to preserve the existing housing which is decent, safe, and sanitary by either encouraging the present owner to move these units to his remainder lands or by making the units available to the public for relocation to another site.
Those displacees who cannot or who do not wish to retain their existing homes will be encouraged to build new replacement homes and will be offered supplemental payments for this purpose in accordance with existing laws.
As required by federal regulation, a relocation program plan has been submitted to the Federal Highway Administration and has been approved by them and by the Wisconsin Department of Local Affairs and Development. This plan is contained in Appendix A.
Upon completion of the proposed project, a detailed analysis will be made of the net effect this project had on the housing market. Such analysis will consider housing units destroyed, units moved and units constructed by displacees.
In the event that the above analysis reveals that these projects have had a negative effect on the existing housing market, the Division of Highways will arrange to replace those units removed from the market. Replacement will be accomplished by the appropriate State agency (not determined as of now).
